class.name: MidiClip
class.brief_description: A piece of MIDI on a beat timeline: an imported MIDI file, or a pattern built in code.
class.description: A [MidiDriver] plays it: [method MidiDriver.place_clip] puts it on the song's timeline, [method MidiDriver.play_clip] plays it from a moment on. [b]From a file:[/b] a [code].mid[/code] (Standard MIDI File, MIDI 1.0) or [code].midi2[/code] (MIDI Clip File, MIDI 2.0) in the project is imported as a [MidiClip], so [code]load("res://music/theme.mid")[/code] gives one, and an exported game carries the clip rather than the file. [method load_file] reads one at run time from anywhere, a [code]user://[/code] folder say. [codeblock] var song: MidiClip = load("res://music/theme.mid") midi.set_channel_target(1, $Piano.stream) midi.place_clip(song) midi.play() [/codeblock] [b]A pattern in code:[/b] values in the clip's [member midi_version] range, positions and lengths in beats. [codeblock] var beat := MidiClip.new() beat.length = 4.0 for i in 4: beat.add_note(i, 10, 36, 110, 0.25) # a kick on every beat, channel 10 beat.add_note(1.0, 10, 38, 100, 0.25) # and a snare on 2 midi.play_clip(beat, midi.next(4.0), 0) # from the next bar, for ever [/codeblock] Positions are in beats, so a clip plays at any tempo; a file's own tempo map is kept beside the events (see [method get_tempo_map]). Notes are stored whole, with their length, so a clip started in the middle still ends every note it starts. Values are held at MIDI 2.0 resolution inside, whatever the file's version, so a clip of either version plays on a driver of either version. Editing a clip that a part is playing leaves that part as it was: the next [method MidiDriver.place_clip] or [method MidiDriver.play_clip] plays the edit. What a file reader keeps: notes, controllers, pitch bend, pressures, program changes (with a MIDI 2.0 program's bank as bank select), tempo, time signature and track names. What it skips: SysEx, groups (everything plays on channels 1-16), and MIDI 2.0 per-note controllers and pitch bend.

method.name: add_event
method.description: Adds a message other than a note at [param beat]: [param kind] is [constant MidiDriver.EVENT_CONTROL] (with [param index] the controller), [constant MidiDriver.EVENT_PITCH_BEND], [constant MidiDriver.EVENT_POLY_PRESSURE] (with [param index] the note), [constant MidiDriver.EVENT_CHANNEL_PRESSURE] or [constant MidiDriver.EVENT_PROGRAM] (with [param value] the program). [param value] is in this clip's MIDI version's range, as [MidiDriver] takes it. The clip grows to reach it.

method.name: add_note
method.description: Adds a note at [param beat], [param length] beats long, on [param channel] (1-16), with [param velocity] in this clip's MIDI version's range (1 and up: 0 is no note). The clip's [member length] grows to reach its end. [param track] groups events, for [method MidiPart.set_track_muted].

method.name: clear
method.description: Removes every event, tempo and meter, and sets [member length] to 0. [member midi_version] stays.

method.name: from_bytes
method.description: Reads a MIDI file from its bytes: a Standard MIDI File or a MIDI Clip File, told apart by their first bytes. Returns [code]null[/code], with an error printed, for anything else, or a damaged file.

method.name: get_bpm
method.description: The first tempo of the clip's tempo map, or 120 if it has none (the files' own default).

method.name: get_event_count
method.description: How many events the clip holds; a note counts once.

method.name: get_events
method.description: Every event, in order, as a [Dictionary] with [code]beat[/code], [code]length[/code] (notes only), [code]track[/code], [code]kind[/code] (a [enum MidiDriver.EventKind]), [code]channel[/code], [code]index[/code] (the note or controller) and [code]value[/code], in this clip's MIDI version's range.

method.name: get_tempo_map
method.description: The tempo changes, as a [Dictionary] each with [code]beat[/code] and [code]bpm[/code]. Played with [method MidiDriver.place_clip], they set the driver's tempo, each on its exact beat.

method.name: load_file
method.description: Reads a MIDI file from [param path]: [code]res://[/code], [code]user://[/code] or an absolute path. Returns [code]null[/code], with an error printed, if it cannot be read or is not a MIDI file. In the project, [code]load()[/code] does the same through the importer.

method.name: set_meter
method.description: A time signature from [param beat] on: [param numerator] over [param denominator], a power of two. The first one decides how long a bar is, which a file's [member length] is rounded up to.

method.name: set_tempo
method.description: A tempo change at [param beat], replacing one already there.

members.member: Storage: the events packed as numbers, seven per event. Saved with the clip, not shown in the inspector; read them with [method get_events].

How long the clip is, in beats: a repeat starts again after it. A file's length is its end rounded up to a whole bar; a pattern's grows as notes are added, and may be set by hand (a one-bar pattern whose last note ends early, say).
Storage: the time signatures packed as numbers.

1 or 2: the version a file stated (a [code].mid[/code] is always 1; a MIDI Clip File is 2 if it holds any MIDI 2.0 message), and the range [method add_note] and [method add_event] take values in. It changes no values held: they are at full resolution inside.
Storage: the tempo map packed as numbers.
The tracks' names, from the file's track name events, in order; empty strings for tracks without one.
